description: Side tile of a three-by-three cul-de-sac: one arc of the 5.5 m turning circle bulging in from its E edge, bare asphalt either side.

image.prompt:
A SEAMLESSLY TILING TOP-DOWN GROUND TEXTURE. This is a flat material swatch, not a photograph of a scene or of an object. The camera looks straight down at the ground from directly overhead, perfectly orthographic, with no perspective, no horizon, no vanishing point and no tilt.

The surface: Flat square of plain unmarked asphalt road surface seen as a single unbroken sheet, no lane markings, no kerb, no sidewalk, no drains and no covers, edge to edge asphalt only Materials: Seamlessly tiling patched grey-black asphalt identical in tone, aggregate and grain to the Plain Asphalt Road Tile, dark tar crack seams and rectangular pothole patches, faint tyre-polish lanes, thin dust and oil spotting; a single solid white edge line bulging in from one edge as a wide circular arc and returning to the same edge, bare asphalt on both sides of it; chalky worn white road paint thinned and scuffed where wheels cross it, edges slightly ragged, no raised relief; the asphalt must wrap on all four edges and every marking must continue across the edges it reaches so that a run of tiles gives one unbroken line with no seam.

Scale: the square shown covers exactly 8 by 8 metres of real ground, so every stone, block, slab, joint, marking, rut and tuft in it is drawn at its true size relative to that. Do not zoom in on a detail and do not pull back to show a wider scene.

Tiling: the texture must repeat seamlessly on all four edges. What runs off the left edge continues onto the right edge, and what runs off the top continues onto the bottom, exactly. No feature may be cut in half at an edge without its other half appearing at the opposite edge. Laid out four by four this must read as one continuous surface with no visible grid, no repeated landmark feature and no seam.

Framing: the surface fills the entire frame edge to edge and corner to corner. There is no border, no frame, no margin, no backdrop, no background, no matte and no empty space of any kind. The ground continues past every edge of the image.

Nothing stands on it and nothing bounds it: no kerb, no wall, no step, no gutter, no drain, no manhole cover, no grass verge, no plants, no people, no vehicles, no furniture, no objects, no litter, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows.

Lighting: flat, even, shadowless overhead illumination, like a lightbox. The image is the surface's true albedo. No sun, no cast shadows, no directional highlights, no specular blowout, no vignette, no gradient across the frame, no baked ambient occlusion in the corners and crevices, no light falloff towards the edges -- an uneven frame cannot tile, because its bright side would meet its dark side at every seam.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, realistic material, real surface wear and staining. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render preview, not a tiled collage of separate photographs, not a pattern illustration.

COMPOSITED AFTERWARDS by scripts/tilekit/composite.mjs, in metres on the 8 m frame: the markings above are deliberately absent from the generated surface. The substrate was NOT regenerated for this tile: it is the Plain Asphalt Road Tile plate (fal-ai/patina/material, seed 80211), already gated by prepare-image --flat, copied so every road tile shares pixel-identical asphalt on every edge; prepare-image was not re-run on the composite because its seam heal would smear a port's lines onto the opposite plain edge.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Cul-de-Sac Bulb Edge
nameTh: ถนนทางตัน วงเวียนกลับรถ ส่วนขอบวง
notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 with NO thickness at all -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. Nothing is modelled: no kerb, no hump, no raised paint, no gutter, no depth of any kind; every marking reads out of the texture. This is a member of the kit's interlocking ROAD TILE family, and every member carries the whole contract so that any tile mates with any other. (1) The footprint is exactly 8 x 8 m on the kit's 8 m grid, pivot base-center so tiles snap on 8 m centres, and a tile is only ever placed at one of the four 90 degree yaws. (2) Every coordinate here is tile-local metres in the texture frame scripts/tilekit/composite.mjs draws in: x runs 0..8 left to right, z runs 0..8 top to bottom, the pivot is at (4, 4), and the four edges are called N (z=0), S (z=8), W (x=0) and E (x=8). (3) Every edge is one of exactly two kinds, a ROAD PORT or PLAIN ASPHALT. A road port mates only with a road port and a plain edge only with a plain edge -- the Plain Asphalt Road Tile, a parking tile, or the plain edge of any other road tile. (4) A road port is always the identical profile: a 6.8 m carriageway from 0.6 to 7.4 across the edge (two 3.4 m lanes), a solid white edge line 0.12 m wide centred at 0.6 and another at 7.4, and a dashed white centre line 0.12 m wide centred at 4.0 with 1.0 m dashes and 1.0 m gaps whose tile boundary falls in the MIDDLE of a gap. On a straight the dashes occupy 0.5-1.5, 2.5-3.5, 4.5-5.5 and 6.5-7.5 along the road, so every port arrives in the same phase and no dash is ever cut by a seam. The 0.6 m outside each edge line is plain asphalt. (5) On a curved centre line the dash unit is scaled so a whole number of dash-gap cycles fits the arc while both ends keep the half-gap phase; every quarter-turn arc in this family therefore uses a dash unit of pi/3 = 1.0472 m. (6) Wherever two edge lines meet at a junction the join is an arc of radius 0.6 m centred on the tile corner, so it passes exactly through both ports' edge-line positions. (7) The asphalt substrate is NOT regenerated for this tile: it is the identical seamless plate of the Plain Asphalt Road Tile, copied, so the asphalt on every edge of every tile is pixel-identical and any edge meets any edge with no join. The markings are then drawn onto it by scripts/tilekit/composite.mjs at the coordinates recorded here, with wrap-around, which is what puts every line in exactly the same place on every tile; prompts.image asks the generator for the bare surface only, and a recipe for this tile id must be added to composite.mjs before its preview is made. Paint is chalky worn white, the lane-marked tile's #d8d5cc at 0.82 opacity, thinned where wheels cross. Thailand drives on the LEFT, so along a N-S road the west lane (x 0.6-4.0) carries traffic heading N and the east lane (x 4.0-7.4) carries traffic heading S; any directional marking follows that. No manhole covers, drain grates, humps, bollards or fixtures of any kind: those are separate props or decals dropped on top. The raised sidewalk is a separate prop placed alongside and is never part of a road tile. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. No destruction groups and no physics: a road tile is static level geometry. The kit's older Road Straight Tile and Road Drain and Utility Tile bake a 1.25 m sidewalk band into the road texture and are a different, incompatible family; never run them in the same street as this one. The two Cul-de-Sac tiles plus plain tiles make one turning circle across a 3 x 3 block (24 x 24 m): Cul-de-Sac Approach in the top-centre cell, Cul-de-Sac Bulb Edge in the left-middle, right-middle and bottom-middle cells (the same tile at yaw 0, 180 and 270/90 so its arc faces the block centre), the Plain Asphalt Road Tile in the centre cell and in the four corner cells. The bulb is a circle of radius 5.5 m (11 m turning diameter, the tight Thai soi size) centred on the block centre, drawn as a single 0.12 m white edge line, and the road enters through the N edge of the approach tile. The radius was chosen so the arc never reaches a corner cell (the nearest corner-cell point is 5.66 m from the centre), which is why the corners are plain tiles rather than a fifth design. Inside the bulb is bare asphalt with no island. Every block edge except the approach's N port is plain asphalt, so the sidewalk prop and other plain tiles sit around it. THIS TILE (left-middle at yaw 0): PORTS: N plain, S plain, W plain; its E edge is an internal seam carrying the arc's two crossings at z=0.23 and z=7.77. GEOMETRY in tile-local metres: one arc of radius 5.5 centred at (12, 4), entering at (8, 0.23), reaching x=6.5 at z=4 and leaving at (8, 7.77) -- a 1.5 m deep bulge. Nothing else is painted. Rotate 180 degrees for the right-middle cell (arc facing W) and 90 degrees for the bottom-middle cell (arc facing N). Asphalt on both sides of the line is plain: inside is the turning circle, outside is the margin the sidewalk prop sits on.
